paper.paper_scope: Investigation of the mechanical properties (hardness, compression, tension and fracture) of Fe–Al–M–C alloys (M = Ti, V, Nb, Ta) based on Fe–15Al and Fe–26Al with strengthening MC carbides and Laves phase, tested at room temperature and elevated temperatures.
paper.title: Mechanical properties of Fe–Al–M–C (M = Ti, V, Nb, Ta) alloys with strengthening carbides and Laves phase

processes.description: All alloys processed by vacuum induction melting and cast into cylindrical copper moulds (32 mm diameter × 186 mm length); no further heat treatment reported. Mechanical test specimens were cut from cast ingots by spark erosion.
processes.processes_notes: Shared processing route for all 12 alloy compositions; room-temperature and elevated-temperature compression/tension tests are characterisation conditions rather than separate terminal material states.

unmapped_findings: Mechanical tests: Brinell hardness (62.5 g load, 2.5 mm ball); compression and tension at deformation rate 10^-4 s^-1; compression tested from room temperature up to 800 °C; tension tested at room temperature, 650 °C and 800 °C; elevated-temperature tests in protective argon with 30 min hold at test temperature (b0018, b0038, b0040).
Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C is three-phase, containing Laves phase (Fe,Al)2Nb besides NbC carbides in the Fe3Al matrix (b0013).

Tension-compression asymmetry observed in all investigated alloys at room temperature and elevated temperatures; Fe-26Al-based alloys show higher asymmetry than Fe-15Al-based alloys (b0029, b0040, b0045).
